source_ref: Gan Y, Tian F, Fan X, Wang H, Zhou J, Yang N, Qi H (2024) Front Endocrinol 15:1390564, doi:10.3389/fendo.2024.1390564 (CC BY; PMC11368761) -- Methods 2.4.3 and Table 2; deposit frontiersin.figshare.com article 26786089, Table1_...xls (md5 2275aac7b5cad4f9bfe5e83df27e2d62); item and option wording from https://dcf.psychiatry.ufl.edu/files/2011/05/HAMILTON-DEPRESSION.pdf (sha256 435b6909a30b169df55e5e461e0f3bd055098d5f8aace8ddb9ca4c4871a43fbe; 'Reference: Hamilton M. A rating scale for depression. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 1960;23:56-62'); processing script data/gan_2024_diabetes_depression.py
note: Item codes ARE the deposit's column names (data/gan_2024_diabetes_depression.py melts ^抑\d+$ by name; no rename, no positional assignment). The .xls has no variable or value labels and no item text (headers are 抑1..抑17 plus 抑162), so there is no level-1 source; the paper names the instrument ('The Hamilton depression scale ... comprises 17 items ... and 5 factors'; 'the 1988 Chinese version') but prints no items. Codes were tied to text by the HAMD-17's own canonical numbering (抑n = item n), with 抑16/抑162 as parts a/b of item 16 (loss of weight), the only split item in the HDRS-17 -- same shape and same canonical source as kokoszka_2022_hamd (batch_064). Checked against the data (Step 5b route 3): summing live items by the Chinese HAMD factor assignments reproduces the paper's Table 2 factor totals exactly -- SA{10,11,12,15,17} 2.019/1.475 vs 2.02/1.475; W{16a+16b} 1.220/1.533 vs 1.22/1.533; CI{2,3,9} 0.645/0.788 vs 0.64/0.788; SU{1,7,8,14} 0.818/1.145 vs 0.82/1.145; SD{4,5,6} 2.374/1.493 vs 2.37/1.493; total 7.173/3.367 vs 7.17/3.367 -- and the deposit's own factor columns (焦虑躯体化, 体重, 认知障碍, 阻滞, 睡眠障碍, 抑郁1) row-for-row for all 318 patients; 0 of 130 cross-factor single swaps still match. Range structure agrees (every item observed above 2 is a canonical 0-4 item) and 抑3 (suicide) is the least-endorsed item of its factor (0.013 vs 0.088, 0.544). Order WITHIN a factor is not tested (PARTIAL). The study's anxiety/somatization factor omits item 13 (the canonical Chinese HAMD factor is 10,11,12,13,15,17); the paper's per-item mean 0.40 = 2.02/5 confirms five items, so this is the authors' definition, not a mapping defect -- 抑13 enters only the total. Both parts of item 16 are rated and both are summed into the weight factor and the total (the form says 'rate either a or b'). Two cells are missing in the deposit (抑1, 抑2, one patient each); the paper and the deposit's factor columns count them as 0, the IRW table omits them. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: Chinese (1988 Chinese version, Chengdu). Zero CJK characters in the paper XML; the deposit's only text is the column codes; Europe PMC supplementaryFiles holds only the figure and the same .xls. So the fallback applies: English canonical form in the base fields, _translated columns empty, language=Chinese. The Chinese version's anchors may differ from the English form (e.g. weekly weight thresholds in jin/kg rather than lb). DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION (as kokoszka_2022_hamd): upper-case stems shipped in sentence case; the form header 'PLEASE COMPLETE THE SCALE BASED ON A STRUCTURED INTERVIEW' kept as a sentence in instructions though this paper does not say a structured interview was used; the instruction clause 'Be sure to record the answers in the appropriate spaces (positions 0 through 4)' omitted as a description of the printed form; en dashes and the 1/2 fraction rendered in ASCII; item 11's symptom list joined into one line. Option rows carry every level the form defines, including resp=3 'Not assessed' on 抑16/抑162, which no respondent used (observed max 2). RIGHTS: register row HAMD (HAM-D-17 original items only) verdict 'ship' (Ben 2026-09-23, irw#2381; 'The HAM-D is in the public domain.') applied, not re-derived; the UFL sheet itself states 'The HDRS is in the public domain.'
public_note: Item text is the canonical English HDRS-17 form; this study administered the 1988 Chinese version and no Chinese wording is published in the deposit or paper, so the English is a substitute rather than the wording raters used. 抑16 and 抑162 are the HDRS's two alternate ratings of item 16 (loss of weight: by patient report vs by weekly measurement); both were scored for every patient and both count in the study's weight factor and total.
